title: Quentin and the Garden
premise: Xanthe Kavanagh has spent nine years poisoning herself in small doses as the crown's food-taster, surviving by being useful and unseen. When the old gods stir beneath the Thornfell mountains, she learns her late mother sold Xanthe's soul to the court below to buy her childhood survival—and the thirteenth moon will be the deadline for its collection. Torn between loyalty to the queen who trusts her and the truth that the court's poisonings are a harvest of souls, Xanthe allies with Quentin, a half-forgotten garden god whose shrine she secretly tended. In the end she trades her immunity—every poison she has absorbed—for Quentin's stolen divinity, breaking her soul-debt but losing her protection, and chooses an unprotected life rooted in truth over invisible survival.
about_author: Wendell Pemberton is a former botanist who left academia to write fantasy steeped in folklore of forgotten shrines and household gods. He lives at the edge of a national forest, where he keeps an overgrown garden he insists is 'mostly feral on purpose.'

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Dish
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. During a state banquet, Xanthe tastes a dish that should kill her—and doesn't, because something old intercepts the poison. She notices the palace gardens blooming out of season around a ruined shrine. Emotional beat: unease; her invisibility, her greatest armor, is beginning to fail.

chapters.title: What the Queen Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The queen privately asks Xanthe to investigate courtiers falling into unexplained trances. Xanthe traces the pattern to deliveries from Thornfell smuggler roads she knows intimately. Emotional beat: conflicted loyalty—the queen's trust warms her even as the task drags her toward danger.

chapters.title: Quentin of the Cracked Urn
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Following the trail, she finds the shrine's occupant: Quentin, a minor god of kitchen gardens, diminished and half-mad from neglect, who recognizes the poison signature as the court-below's work. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; two forgotten creatures recognizing each other.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Among her mother's effects, Xanthe finds the contract: her soul sold to the court beneath the mountain in exchange for the child surviving famine. The thirteenth moon marks collection. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal reframed—her mother's love was real, and it was a transaction.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road South
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin guides Xanthe through the mountain passes using senses she lacks, watching her ration her own safety with brutal efficiency. They evade the court's wraith-toll collectors. Emotional beat: growing trust; Quentin begins to want things again, which terrifies him.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Disguised as a soul-debtor come to negotiate, Xanthe enters the subterranean court and discovers the 'poisonings' above are harvesting prayers and souls to feed the starving old gods. Her own name sits in the ledger, ink still wet. Emotional beat: horror; the enemy is desperate, not merely cruel.

chapters.title: The Bargain She Refuses
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The court offers to void her debt if she betrays the queen—her taster's access makes her the perfect vessel for the final harvest. Meanwhile the queen's spymaster grows suspicious of her absences. Emotional beat: crushing pressure; every loyalty now demands a different betrayal.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. With days left, Quentin reveals the truth he withheld: his stolen divinity was sold to the same court, and restoring him would give Xanthe leverage—but consuming it might destroy what remains of him. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit; both choose each other anyway.

chapters.title: The Harvest Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. At the moon's turn, Xanthe breaks into the ledger-hall, steals back Quentin's soul-shard, and when the court moves to collect hers, she offers instead the accumulated poisons of nine years—a body so saturated with death that no god can digest it. The ledger burns. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Rooted
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Stripped of her immunity, Xanthe confesses everything to the queen and resigns, then returns to the shrine where Quentin, restored but small, plants a garden with her. Survival was never living; this is. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace—an unprotected life, chosen freely.
